answer: A Code contribution signed off by a domain expert backed by a refundable deposit makes identity cost real work: the code contribution is reviewed line by line, the refundable deposit is released only when the work is accepted, and a rejected submission costs the applicant time and money, so a Sybil farm must produce genuine, reviewed output for every fake account it wants. Reviewers look for the echo that does not belong: work with no substance behind it. From the jade to the lantern, the same rule holds: no review, no trust, no exception.
